Michelle Dong 
Michelle Dong is an 
AmeriCorps VISTA at 
UMass Dartmouth 
focused on expanding 
and strengthening 
mentoring initiatives that 
support student success. 
She is a graduate of the 
University at Albany, where she earned a bachelor’s 
degree in Sociology with minors in International 
Studies and Social Welfare. During her senior year, 
Michelle interned with the State University of New York 
(SUNY), an experience that introduced her to higher 
education as a space for advancing equity and student 
support—work that ultimately led her to AmeriCorps 
VISTA service. 
Inspired by the mentors who shaped her own college 
journey, Michelle saw her VISTA role at UMass 
Dartmouth as a natural next step after graduation. In 
her current position, she is developing a sustainable 
peer mentoring program designed to support first- 
generation, first-year students. Her work includes 
learning from existing mentoring efforts on campus, 
researching national best practices, and creating 
training materials for both mentors and mentees. 
The goal of this initiative was to launch a 
comprehensive peer mentoring program during Fall 
2026 that provides first-generation students with the 
guidance, resources, and sense of belonging they need 
to thrive. Through this work, Michelle aims to help 
students build a strong foundation for their university 
experience, persist through graduation, and move 
toward long-term economic mobility.
